**Finding submitted: COMPLIANT (preferred position) — no redline proposed.**

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Classification | Compliant at **preferred** |
| Key evidence | §12.3 (p0051), §2.1 (p0013) |
| Redline | None — rule already satisfied |

**Why compliant:** The single preferred element — "Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation" — is affirmatively met. §12.3 does not merely omit exclusivity; it expressly records that "Nothing restricts Customer from ... engaging any supplier" and that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment." §2.1 backs that up commercially with no minimum quantity or purchase commitment, and confirms that declining to sign a further Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.

**Direction check:** §12.4 restricts *Vendor* from marketing a service competing with our proprietary analytics products. That is an exclusivity-flavoured covenant running in our favour, so per the detection guidance it is preserved and not flagged.

**Coverage of the search:** all detection phrases were run to nil result ("sole supplier", "sole and exclusive provider", "all of its requirements", "shall not procure … from any third party", "preferred/primary supplier", "right of first refusal", "solely from Vendor"). The planner's candidate sections (2, 4, 7, 12) were read in full, plus §13 licence restrictions and §30 general terms. Every remaining "exclusive" hit is unrelated: the non-exclusive licence *to us* (§13.1), exclusive-remedy carve-outs (§19.3, §21.5, §30.2), and exclusive jurisdiction (§28.2).

Because the preferred checklist is satisfied, the fallback elements (defined product category, 12-month cap, automatic exit on service-level or delivery-date failure) are not engaged, and no upgrade drafting is required.
